tagline.text: A day-hike mountain in Cuenca with the Rockies, a rock lookout over Taal Lake

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–1,000 (per person, including transport and guide fee)

children.text: Mount Maculot is a dormant volcano in Cuenca, Batangas, and a popular day hike from Manila. From the Rockies, a rock lookout partway up, Taal Lake and Taal Volcano Island spread out below you.
Mount Maculot rises above the town of Cuenca in Batangas. Its summit is commonly given as
about 930 m

, though some sources list 957 m. It is a dormant stratovolcano on the rim of the Taal Caldera, and many guides describe it as the second-highest peak in Batangas. It is only 2–3 hours from Manila by bus, so many hikers leave before dawn and return the same day.
There are three main sights. The Grotto (a Marian shrine) sits at about
above sea level, the Rockies lookout at about

, and then the summit itself. At the Rockies you stand on projecting rock and look out over Taal Lake, Taal Volcano Island in the middle of it, and the Tagaytay ridge in the distance. It is Maculot's best-known photo spot.

Routes are either an out-and-back along the same trail or a traverse, going up one side and down the other. The traverse passes the Rockies, the summit and the Grotto, and is reported to include rope-assisted climbing and a roped descent in places. Either way, hikers usually register at the outpost at the village entrance and climb with a local guide. Two trails are commonly described. The western trail starts at Don Juan at about
and climbs to the Maculot campsite at about
; from there the left branch leads to Taal Lake viewpoints and the right branch to the summit. The eastern (Grotto) trail starts at Pinagkaisahan at about
and goes straight up to the summit. The two trailheads are only about
1 km
apart, so a loop is possible.
The difficulty is moderate. Beginners can manage it, but the last stretch of about

before the summit is steep, and the rock and mud get slippery after rain. Start before the sun gets strong and go in the dry season. During Holy Week the Grotto draws pilgrims and hikers, and it gets very crowded. One hiking blog recorded a loop of about
9 km
with roughly
of total ascent in
3–4 hours
. It passed the Grotto at about
1.1 km
, the summit at about
2.1 km
and the Rockies at about
3.6 km
. That was a brisk pace, so most visitors should allow 5–7 hours with rests and photo stops. Dogs and mountain bikes are reportedly not allowed.
A rocky ridge at about

. You can see Taal Lake, Taal Volcano Island, the Tagaytay highlands and surrounding islands, and on clear days the mountains toward Manila. The rock at the edge is slippery, so choose sturdy shoes. Hikers report that the Rockies take a little over an hour from the trailhead, and the traverse more than two hours.

blocks.title: The Grotto and the Stations of the Cross

children.text: The path to the Marian shrine passes the 14 Stations of the Cross, and the staircase is said to have roughly 1,000 steps. Some people climb in the early morning and wait at the Grotto for sunrise.
The last

before the summit is steep, with sections where you hold a rope. The summit is wooded, so it rewards you more with a sense of achievement than with a view. Reports give its height as 930 m or 957 m, likely because of different measurement standards.

Hikers report frequent mist and light rain in the mid-mountain forest, creating a damp microclimate. It is cool but slippery, a contrast to the late-morning sun. On sunny days the same trail feels much hotter, so pass this section early in the morning.
A store at the campsite below the Rockies sells snacks and drinks. Hikers mention instant noodles topped with an egg as a favorite, and vendors near the summit are said to sell coconut drinks.
Going up one side and coming down toward the Grotto lets you see the Rockies, the summit and the Grotto in one trip. The descent is a long concrete staircase that is hard on the knees.
Board a bus bound for Lemery from Buendia or Pasay in Manila.
Get off in Cuenca, ride a tricycle to the trailhead (Mountaineer's Store), and register and arrange a guide at the outpost.
Start hiking. The campsite is about
1 hour 30 minutes
away.
Climb the Rockies for the view, then return to the campsite for breakfast.
Set off for the summit, which takes about
1 hour 15 minutes
Descend toward the Grotto and have an early lunch.
Reach the exit point, wash up and take a tricycle into Cuenca town.
These times are an example based on one travel blogger's 2018 itinerary. Your pace and the weather will change them.
Register at the Cuenca trailhead and set off.
Pass the campsite and reach the Rockies ridge.
Enjoy the view and descend the way you came.
Skipping the summit saves a lot of time and energy.
Take a bus bound for Lemery from the terminal at Buendia (near LRT Gil Puyat Station) or from PITX, and get off in Cuenca town. The trip takes about
2–3 hours
According to a 2018 blog, the fare was about ₱147, and it may be higher now. The first buses leave around 3:00 AM.
On the way back, taking a bus from SM Lipa toward Manila (EDSA Shaw) takes
2–4 hours
, depending heavily on traffic.
By car it takes roughly 1.5–2 hours from Manila. This comes from hiker reports and varies with traffic.
A tricycle from Cuenca town to the trailhead takes about
10–15 minutes
. The fare used to be about ₱20, but today you will need to negotiate.
If you finish the traverse, you will need another tricycle from the exit point to town.
A common route is a jeepney from Cuenca town to Lipa, then to SM Lipa, where you transfer to a bus to Manila.
Bus schedules and fares change, so check them before you leave.
The dry season from November to May is best. When it rains, the trail turns to mud and the rocks become dangerous.

Starting before dawn is practically a must. The midday sun is strong, and there is little shade near the summit and the Grotto. Registration and the trailhead get long lines during Holy Week and on weekends.
In the rainy season the forest section often has mist and rain, and the trail stays muddy for days afterward. Many hikers report that weekdays are much quieter than weekends on the narrow sections.

Most people do it as a day trip, so few stay in Cuenca. There are lodgings and restaurants in Cuenca town and nearby Lipa City, and you can also sleep in Lemery or elsewhere in Batangas the night before and arrive at dawn.

On the mountain you can buy snacks and drinks at the campsite store and from vendors. After the hike, a bowl of Batangas lomi or another hot soup at a restaurant in Cuenca town is a good way to finish.
Buy water and snacks in Cuenca town before you start, and bring plenty of cash. The store on the mountain and the tricycle drivers mostly accept cash only.

The Grotto is a Catholic Marian shrine, so many pilgrims visit during Holy Week. Keep quiet and dress and behave respectfully at the shrine. The stores and the trail are busier than usual during the pilgrimage, so it helps to move early in the morning.
Wear hiking shoes that hold your feet firmly. Sandals and worn-out sneakers are dangerous on the rocky sections.
If you catch a bus around 3:00 AM and start at about 5:00, you avoid the sun and can see the view from the Rockies around sunrise.
Carry 1.5–2 liters of water per person. There is little shade near the summit and the Grotto.
Thorny bushes can scratch you, so bring antiseptic and bandages.
There are places to wash up after the hike, so a change of clothes and a towel are handy.
Take your trash home, and support local people such as the store owners and guides.
Ask in the village about the last ride back so you finish before transport stops.
Weekdays are less crowded on the narrow sections and the registration line is shorter than on weekends.
Small roadside stores mostly open on weekends and some are closed on weekdays, so bring water and snacks in advance.
A 2018 report put the total of bus, tricycle, registration and a guide fee shared by five at about ₱500–600 per person. Prices have risen since, so prepare up to ₱1,000 to be safe.
Right after rain or during the rainy season, the rocks and mud trail are slippery and accidents are common, so it is best to postpone.
The last
before the summit is steep and needs a rope in places. Depending on your fitness and the weather, stopping at the Rockies instead of the summit is perfectly fine.
Do not stand too close to the edge of the Rockies while taking photos, as you could fall.

The descent from the Grotto is a long staircase that is hard on weak knees. Hiking with a guide is the norm and some sources say it is required, so register at the trailhead outpost and hire a guide rather than going alone.
During Holy Week, registration and the trail are very crowded, so check local announcements for any limits. Guide fees and registration rules can change, so check the latest notice.
There is little shade near the summit and the Grotto, so heatstroke is a risk in the daytime. Bring a hat and water.
The island volcano in the lake that you look down on from the Rockies. Access may be restricted depending on its activity, so check the latest notice.
A highland resort town on the ridge across Taal Lake. A good place to rest after the hike.
A historic town with Spanish colonial buildings.
Another popular day-hike mountain near Manila, on the Nasugbu side.
